analysis.note: Negates jāyate.
Intransitive present, ‘is born/arises’; Śaṅkara glosses notpadyate.
Intransitive middle present, ‘dies’.
Here not disjunctive ‘or’ but cārtha, ‘and/also’, according to Śaṅkara.
Śaṅkara says it is connected with all denials of modification.

verification.detail: avyaya not in kosha or MW

analysis.note: Sandhied with ayam as nāyaṃ.
Masculine nominative singular pronoun referring to the ātmā.
Absolutive/gerund from √bhū: ‘having been / having come to be’.
Periphrastic future 3rd singular: ‘will be / will come to be’; Śaṅkara’s gloss uses the parallel agent-future gantā.
Used by Śaṅkara to supply the alternative abhūtvā vā bhavitā.
Negates the future-being construction in the double denial explained by Śaṅkara.
Adverbial ‘again’; Śaṅkara glosses with punaḥ.
‘Unborn’; Śaṅkara derives it from the denial of jāyate.

verification.detail: compound stem aja as Pum/Prathama/Eka: pass; relation tatpurusa: unsupported (logged)

analysis.note: ‘Eternal’; Śaṅkara derives it from the denial of mriyate.
Śaṅkara takes this as denying decay/decline, apakṣaya.
Masculine nominative singular pronoun; again refers to the ātmā.
Not merely ‘old/worn out’: Śaṅkara explains purāpi nava eva, denying growth/increase.
Negates the passive verb hanyate.
Passive present, but Śaṅkara states that √han is to be understood here in the sense of vipariṇāma, ‘transformation’, not literal killing.
Locative singular neuter present passive participle from √han, agreeing with śarīre; with śarīre forms a locative absolute.
Locative singular: ‘when/in the body’; part of the locative absolute hanyamāne śarīre.

justifications.decision: The verse’s masculine pronoun is not taken as the body or the empirical person; Śaṅkara repeatedly identifies the subject as ayam ātmā and says all worldly transformations are denied in the ātmā.
options_considered: ayam as a merely deictic ‘this one’ without identifying the referent
ayam as the body or embodied empirical person
ayam as the ātmā taught in the preceding context
justifications.chosen: ayam refers to the ātmā, so the translation says ‘this Self (ātman)’.

evidence.quote: yasmāt ayam ātmā bhūtvā bhavana-kriyām anubhūya paścāt abhavitā abhāvaṃ gantā na bhūyaḥ punaḥ, tasmāt na mriyate |
evidence.translation: Because this is ‘this ātman’, Śaṅkara identifies the subject of the clause as the Self.

evidence.quote:
asmin mantre ṣaḍ-bhāva-vikārā laukika-vastu-vikriyā ātmani pratiṣidhyante |
sarva-prakāra-vikriyā-rahita ātmā iti vākyārthaḥ |
evidence.translation: In this mantra the six modes of worldly change are denied in the ātman; the sentence-meaning is that the ātman is free from every kind of transformation.

justifications.decision: The first vā is rendered conjunctively, not as a genuine alternative ‘or’; kadācit is construed with the denials of birth and death, indeed with the denials of all transformations.
options_considered: kadācit modifying all denials of transformation
justifications.chosen: ‘He is not born, and he does not die, ever.’

evidence.quote:
na jāyate notpadyate, jani-lakṣaṇā vastu-vikriyā na ātmano vidyate ity arthaḥ |
tathā na mriyate vā |
vā-śabdaḥ cārthe |
na mriyate ca iti antyā vināśa-lakṣaṇā vikriyā pratiṣidhyate |
evidence.translation: ‘He is not born’ means no birth-type modification exists in the Self; likewise he does not die. The word vā has the sense of ca, ‘and’, and the final destruction-type modification is denied.

evidence.quote: kadācic chabdaḥ sarva-vikriyā-pratiṣedhaiḥ saṃbadhyate -- na kadācit jāyate, na kadācit mriyate, ity evam |
evidence.translation: The word kadācit is connected with all the denials of transformation: never is he born, never does he die, and so on.

justifications.decision: The compact second pāda is expanded following Śaṅkara into a twofold denial: the Self is not something that, after being, goes to non-being; nor is it like a body, something that, after non-being, comes into being. Bhūyaḥ is taken as ‘again’ (punaḥ).
options_considered: only ‘having been, he will be again’
only ‘having once existed, he will not exist again’
a twofold Śaṅkara-style denial of both post-existence non-being and prior-nonbeing-to-being
justifications.chosen: ‘Nor, after having been, will this one fail to be again; nor, after not having been, will he come to be again.’

evidence.quote: yasmāt ayam ātmā bhūtvā bhavana-kriyām anubhūya paścāt abhavitā abhāvaṃ gantā na bhūyaḥ punaḥ, tasmāt na mriyate |
evidence.translation: Śaṅkara explains the death-denial: the Self is not one that, after having been, later goes to non-existence; bhūyaḥ is glossed as punaḥ, ‘again’.

evidence.quote:
vā-śabdāt na-śabdāc ca ayam ātmā abhūtvā vā bhavitā dehavat na bhūyaḥ |
tasmāt na jāyate |
yo hi abhūtvā bhavitā sa jāyata ity ucyate |
evidence.translation: From vā and na Śaṅkara also supplies the birth-denial: the Self is not, like a body, one that after not having been will come to be again; one that does so is said to be born.

justifications.decision: The adjectives are not mere epithets. Śaṅkara correlates them with the denial of specific bhāva-vikāras: birth, death, decline, and growth. Purāṇa therefore cannot mean ‘old/worn out’ in the ordinary sense; it is ‘old’ while remaining ever new, because the partless Self does not increase.
options_considered: śāśvata as a generic synonym of nitya only
the adjectives as technical denials of specific transformations
justifications.chosen: ajaḥ, nityaḥ, śāśvataḥ, purāṇaḥ are rendered as ‘unborn, eternal, undecaying, ancient-yet-ever-new’.

evidence.quote: yasmād evaṃ tasmāt ajaḥ, yasmāt na mriyate tasmāt nityaś ca |
evidence.translation: Because the Self is not born, it is ajaḥ; because it does not die, it is nityaḥ.

evidence.quote:
yadyapi ādy-antayor vikriyayoḥ pratiṣedhe sarvā vikriyāḥ pratiṣiddhā bhavanti, tathāpi madhya-bhāvinīnāṃ vikriyāṇāṃ sva-śabdair eva pratiṣedhaḥ kartavyo 'nuktānām api yauvanādi-samasta-vikriyāṇāṃ pratiṣedho yathā syāt ity āha-- śāśvata ity ādinā |
śāśvata iti apakṣaya-lakṣaṇā vikriyā pratiṣidhyate |
śaśvad-bhavaḥ śāśvataḥ |
na apakṣīyate svarūpeṇa, niravayavatvāt |
nāpi guṇa-kṣayeṇa apakṣayaḥ, nirguṇatvāt |
evidence.translation: Although denying beginning and end already denies all transformations, the middle transformations are denied by their own words. Śāśvata denies the transformation called decline; the Self does not decline in its own nature or through loss of qualities.

evidence.quote:
apakṣaya-viparītāpi vṛddhi-lakṣaṇā vikriyā pratiṣidhyate --- purāṇa iti |
yo hi avayavāgamena upacīyate sa vardhate abhinava iti ca ucyate |
ayaṃ tu ātmā niravayavatvāt purāpi nava eveti purāṇaḥ na vardhate ity arthaḥ |
evidence.translation: Purāṇa denies the opposite of decline, namely growth. What grows by the addition of parts is called new; but this partless Self is even formerly new—purāṇa—and so does not grow.

justifications.decision: Although the surface verb is from √han, Śaṅkara explicitly says that here √han must be understood in the sense of vipariṇāma in order to avoid repetition after mriyate. The locative absolute therefore means ‘when the body is being transformed’.
options_considered: vipariṇāma, transformation/change, as Śaṅkara’s intended sense
justifications.chosen: hanyate and hanyamāne are translated by ‘is transformed / being transformed’, not by literal ‘is slain / being slain’.

evidence.quote:
tathā na hanyate |
hantiḥ atra vipariṇāmārthe draṣṭavyo 'punaruktatāyai |
na vipariṇamyate ity arthaḥ |
evidence.translation: Similarly, ‘he is not hanyate’; here han is to be seen as having the meaning of transformation, to avoid repetition. The meaning is: he is not transformed.

one_shot_delta: A commentary-blind translation would likely render vā as ‘or’; Śaṅkara says the first vā has the force of ca, ‘and’.
It might attach kadācit only to ‘dies’; Śaṅkara attaches it to all the denials of transformation.

It might flatten nāyaṃ bhūtvā bhavitā vā na bhūyaḥ into only one existential claim; Śaṅkara extracts a twofold denial, covering both death as becoming non-existent after being and birth as coming into being after non-being.
It might translate purāṇa simply as ‘old’; Śaṅkara requires the paradoxical sense ‘ancient yet ever new’, because the partless Self does not grow.

It would almost certainly translate hanyate/hanyamāne as ‘is slain/when the body is slain’; Śaṅkara explicitly takes √han here as vipariṇāma, ‘transformation’, to avoid repeating the earlier denial of death.
analyzer_disagreements: mriyate: ByT5 marks Pv; I analyze √mṛ mriyate as an intransitive middle present in Kartari prayoga, ‘dies’, not a passive ‘is died’.
bhavitā: ByT5’s SFu tag is treated as too broad/misleading for this form; I specify luṭ/periphrastic future 3rd singular, supported by Śaṅkara’s gantā gloss at line 6.
kadācit: ByT5 segments kadācid; the printed sandhi is kadācin before nāyaṃ, while the pausal/pre-sandhi form required here is kadācit.
open_questions: Commentary line 25 in the supplied plaintext appears to read śarīrāḥ where the verse and construction require śarīre; I treat this as a plaintext error, not as a meaningful variant.
mula: na jāyate mriyate vā kadācin nāyaṃ bhūtvā bhavitā vā na bhūyaḥ | ajo nityaḥ śāśvato 'yaṃ purāṇo na hanyate hanyamāne śarīre
